title: Layers around a message
description:
Show how each layer wraps the one above it.

```
application: GET / HTTP/1.1 (16 bytes)
transport:   [TCP 20][16]                  36 bytes
network:     [IP 20][TCP 20][16]           56 bytes
link:        [ETH 14][IP 20][TCP 20][16][FCS 4]  74 bytes
overhead: 58 bytes for 16 bytes of data (78%)
```
hints: Each layer adds its header in front and its trailer behind; the size grows by `header + trailer` (lesson 1.01).
The overhead percentage is `(total - payload) * 100 / total`.
requirements: A `struct Layer { std::string name; int header; int trailer; };` table for TCP, IP and Ethernet.
Wrap the payload layer by layer, printing the size at each step.
Compare TCP with UDP (8-byte header) for the same message.
stretch: Work out how many full-size (1500-byte) packets a 1 MB file needs, and the total overhead.
